title: AIRS Medical secures FDA clearance for MRI software
source_used: AIRS Medical press release on PR Newswire (AuntMinnie, the pool's outlet, is blocked)
key_facts: AIRS Medical announced on 5 Oct 2026 (Chicago, via PR Newswire) that the US FDA has granted 510(k) clearance for SwiftSight Body Composition.

The AI software quantifies muscle and fat from MRI images, including visceral and subcutaneous fat, abdominal and thigh muscle, muscle quality and left-right muscle balance, plus liver fat measured as proton density fat fraction.
It is built around an MRI scan of under five minutes followed by automated AI analysis; results are benchmarked against age- and sex-matched reference populations in one Body Composition Report.
SimonMed Imaging will be the first customer to deploy it.
AIRS Medical describes itself as an MRI intelligence company; its portfolio includes SwiftMR (AI MRI reconstruction) and SwiftSight (a quantitative MRI platform).
The company's roadmap lists diffusion tensor imaging for Nov 2026 and quantitative joint applications for 2027.
The release gives no accuracy or clinical-performance figures.
quote_evidence: AIRS Medical today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has granted 510(k) clearance for SwiftSight® Body Composition, expanding the company's quantitative MRI platform into body composition analysis.
SimonMed Imaging will be the first customer to deploy the newly cleared solution.
SwiftSight Body Composition is designed around a scan of less than five minutes, followed by automated AI analysis.
why_it_matters_hint: An MRI-based body-fat, muscle and liver-fat measurement tool gets FDA clearance, announced by the maker with no accuracy data.
